verified_boundaries: Wrong proposal digest, changed descriptor, changed authority and stale proposal reject before KeySource.as_sign is called
Nightly credentials cannot sign Release, targets, snapshot or timestamp under the independently selected test authority
Two-key Release threshold rejects missing, repeated and foreign keys; extra supplied authority is refused
Each original KeySource is loaded once; original credentials are not reopened during signing
Canonical signature/object order produces identical Ed25519 metadata with reversed key input order and independently randomized signer maps
Channel append/renew preserves prior boot-compatible targets and prevents known generation/identity reassignment
Snapshot/timestamp references reject lower versions and changed bytes at the same version
Expired/changed/invalid policy, future-dated proposals, oversized inputs and exhausted versions reject
Requests cannot contain a root-signing operation, policy changes or unknown executable/path fields
Independently signed roles form a feed accepted by both Release/Nightly TrustStore consumers and publication.inventory; Release promotion retains original payload and generation
limitations: Authority and parent inputs must come from independently selected current publisher state; signatures alone do not establish freshness.
Admitted proposal hashes do not prove GitHub workflow identity, artifact provenance, source CI, expanded-image validation or maintainer approval.
The signing helper does not establish job/secret isolation or historical generation allocation; those caller controls are still required.
This operation appends or renews catalogs, not pruning or credential/root rotation.
A reserved publication must retain original signed outputs, especially for randomized signature algorithms.
All private credentials used in tests were ephemeral and confined to test memory or temporary directories. No production signing material was created.
